lots.what_it_is: Set of six George III sterling silver Old English pattern teaspoons, London, attributed by Gowans to Thomas & William Chawner 1768; 72.8g total, 12cm each, bottom-marked stems, engraved initials.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 4 (enlarged): lion passant clear, a faint worn middle mark, and a maker's mark reading as script T/W C, consistent with Thomas & William Chawner. No legible date letter; bottom-marked London spoons of this period often carried only lion and maker, so the '1768' date may be Gowans' attribution rather than a read date letter. Photo 3: marks on another spoon very worn. Photo 5: bright-cut-free plain terminals engraved 'A over C I' and 'W' between stars, so the six are probably not all one original set (different initials). Photo 1: bowls with drop, general polish wear, light scratching; no obvious splits or repairs seen at this size.
lots.condition: Worn marks, polish wear and scratches, different engraved initials on at least two spoons (possibly assembled set); no visible repairs in the photos.
